pages.title: AI.fred
pages.summary: The venture in two pages: the promise, the human-in-the-gap model, the two fatal failures and how the design makes them structurally impossible, the three-market shape, what exists today, and how to read this publication.

pages.title: 00 Thesis
pages.summary: Why AI.fred wins where the flat-fee concierge players cannot follow: the customer and the high-consequence wedge, why now, India as build base with the US and UK as commercial ground, the researched landscape in India, the US and the UK, and the trust architecture as the moat.

pages.title: 01 Product
pages.summary: The product as the user meets it: journeys across six verticals, the task taxonomy, intake through a channel-agnostic gateway (channel amber), the authority envelope, the two-loop verdict system, onboarding and context capture, and what we refuse to do.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.summary: The harness an engineer builds first: the component map, the planner, the classifier and the step-type catalogue, the execution surfaces and their controllers, the task state machine with its invariant, verification and the evidence pipeline, the context store, the intake gateway behind the vault's edge proxy, and the market adapter model.

pages.title: Worker console
pages.summary: The operator's task-card view, the alias-only rule, the structured outcome codes, dual control from the worker's side, the exceptions board, and the state-machine invariant identical to 02.

pages.title: 03 Trust and data
pages.summary: How nobody on our side ever sees a real value: the alias and vault model, the substitution component, the execution surfaces, artefact redaction, the passports, the policy flags, the threat model as named and closed paths, the access ledger, the residency map and the privacy-law skeleton.

pages.title: The trust story
pages.summary: One page a customer could read: what AI.fred does, why nobody who works for us ever sees your numbers, what your ledger looks like, and what we never do.

pages.title: 04 Operations
pages.summary: How the floor runs: need-to-know task cards, three worker tiers with dual control, a 24-hour wheel of three shifts from one office, site controls as part of the trust guarantee, QA as a shift duty, and service levels stated qualitatively. No cost model.

pages.title: 05 Business
pages.summary: The economics, no longer deferred: the five-tier task model that sets cost, human minutes per user per month as the governing ratio, the cost split, sixty months of simulated paths, the round plan and the geography gates. Every number modelled rather than measured.

pages.title: Measurement protocol
pages.summary: The thirty-task instrument that replaces the priors in 05: the five-outcome rubric scored on positive evidence, the timing definitions, the task set, the run protocol, the learning-curve sub-test and the decision thresholds set in advance.

pages.title: The model
pages.summary: A short description of the unit model and the Monte Carlo simulation behind 05: the scenarios, the run and seed the publication quotes, where the files sit, and the limits of the method.

pages.title: 06 Roadmap
pages.summary: The harness-first build sequence in eight gated stages, the pilot scoped by capability rather than headcount, the build-versus-buy table with what each purchase commits us to, and the three-part playbook for entering a country.

pages.title: 07 Open items
pages.summary: Every open item with an owner and a trigger: the channel amber, first-cohort sequencing, the legal to-verifies, Netlify access, naming, the make-good policy, remote-safe operations, vendor choices, and the objections formed against fixed decisions during the build.

pages.title: DR-001 Channel-agnostic intake gateway; WhatsApp front door amber
pages.summary: One intake gateway, behind the vault's tokenising edge proxy, normalises every channel into one internal request format; which channel opens the front door in each market is amber until the first US/UK cohort is scoped.

pages.title: DR-002 Verdict system split into a control loop and an improvement loop
pages.summary: Structured outcome codes decide whether a step is closed; the user's one-tap verdict, five options and no more, is the only measure of quality and the only thing that closes a task.

pages.title: DR-003 Full delegation as the capability ceiling, with per-jurisdiction policy flags
pages.summary: The harness is designed to the full ceiling, identity acts included; a per-jurisdiction policy layer decides at runtime what is delegated, what bounces and what is prohibited. Supersedes the A/B/C capability-tier framing.

pages.title: DR-004 The authority envelope and the point-of-no-return test
pages.summary: Every task carries one authority envelope; delegation is total inside it and impossible outside it, and every step is sorted by a point-of-no-return test into execute, dual control or bounce.

pages.title: DR-005 An explicit task state machine, with lapsed distinct from withdrawn
pages.summary: Every task lives in an explicit state machine with live timers and recorded transitions; user silence ends in lapsed through visible nudges, lapsed is not withdrawn, and system silence is an exception the watchdog surfaces.

pages.title: DR-006 Office-mandatory 24/7 operation with site controls
pages.summary: Workers execute only from premises of ours, on our devices. The attested 24-hour site with three shifts is the shape at scale: a small controlled room carries the pilot, and the site arrives when a foreign market goes live or the floor passes a headcount threshold the founder has yet to set. Site controls remain part of the trust guarantee.

pages.title: DR-007 A universal core with per-country adapters, legal pack and shift
pages.summary: One country-agnostic harness carries every trust property; each market adds passport adapters to its rails, a legal pack, a data-residency map and a shift, and expansion is that playbook repeated.

pages.title: DR-008 Tokenisation vault bought, not built
pages.summary: Real values live in a bought, regionally hosted tokenisation vault of the Skyflow, VGS and Basis Theory class; everything of ours handles aliases. Why the layer is bought, what buying does not delegate, and why no vendor is chosen yet.

pages.title: DR-009 Evidence redaction as part of the harness
pages.summary: Every screenshot, recording, transcript and DOM capture is redacted inside the harness before it is stored and verified by a second pass that fails closed; no raw artefact is ever human-viewable, and the evidence system is treated as a leak path.

pages.title: DR-010 Plain HTML with no build step
pages.summary: The publication is plain static HTML served straight from GitHub by Netlify with no build command, framework, CDN or external asset. HTML is the single canonical source; a static site generator and Markdown-canonical generation were rejected because two representations drift.

pages.title: DR-011 A visual token-and-component system
pages.summary: Every colour, type role and spacing value is a token defined once; every component is defined once and composed on every page; no page carries styling of its own. A framework and per-page styling were rejected, and the harness enforces the rule.

pages.title: DR-012 The design plan: an engineering dossier
pages.summary: The visual system for the publication: palette, type, numbering voice, page kinds, components, diagram language and print, critiqued against the generic defaults and fixed.

pages.title: DR-013 The verification standard for this edition
pages.summary: In this edition a verified chip means the claim was checked against a search-engine excerpt of the named, dated source, because the build environment blocked full page reads and capped searches; no page circulates externally before its load-bearing sources are re-read.

pages.title: DR-014 The substitution framing: boundary sequence over ledger spine
pages.summary: Sections 1 to 4 of 03 are organised as a boundary sequence, one real value followed across five boundaries with Figure 3.2 as the substitution sequence; the ledger-led framing was rejected as the spine and grafted for its best parts.

pages.title: DR-015 Economics deferred to post-Series A/B
pages.summary: Task economics, pricing and unit costs are deferred by the founder's ruling to after a Series A or B. The 05 stub states the deferral and its trigger; no other page carries a price, a cost or a margin. Modelling now was rejected because every number would be invented.

pages.title: DR-016 The context store as a temporal knowledge graph
pages.summary: The user's profile is a temporal knowledge graph in the Graphiti style: every fact carries its source, date, validity interval, confidence and whether the user confirmed it; sensitive fields are aliases held in the vault. A flat profile table and a document store without temporal validity were rejected.

pages.title: DR-017 A dependency map of the record, kept as a tool
pages.summary: The dependencies inside this publication are mapped as one graph of typed edges and faceted nodes, kept as a tool under the repository's tools directory, with one served view of it under docs/depmap/ and no other page; a node names a decision, a mechanism, an invariant or a closed list and points at the places the pages state it, and the harness checks every pointer on every pass.

pages.title: DR-018 Mail sent from the user's own address
pages.summary: Every email a third party receives for a user comes from the user's own address: sent by the relay under a send scope the user grants, or written by the harness and sent by the user from their own mail app; replies reach us by the read connector or the user's forward, and the per-task address at our domain is inbound only.

pages.title: DR-019 The endgame is the starting scope
pages.summary: What the previous record called the endgame is the starting scope: the whole of a personal economic life from the first day, with the consequential tasks as the hook. Data sold as an asset is withdrawn; product improvement and a commerce take rate survive.

pages.title: DR-020 Everyday tasks in scope from day one
pages.summary: The product serves the user's everyday economic life and their consequential institutional tasks from launch, in one subscription, without staging.

pages.title: DR-021 Telephony masking dropped; no value is ever spoken
pages.summary: No value held in the vault is ever spoken on a call, in either direction; the audio masking pipeline, the media server and the specialist hire are dropped, and phone work covers non-authenticating calls only.

pages.title: DR-022 Structured task cards replace pixel masking
pages.summary: For modelled workflows the worker is given a structured task card rather than a stream of pixels, with values placed at submit; pixel streaming is deferred as the fallback and the workflow library becomes load-bearing.

pages.title: DR-023 Geography sequencing and the entity thresholds
pages.summary: The United Kingdom opens between months 8 and 14 with acquisition moved there, India is the delivery base, and two gates govern any market: 400 users in the UK and 600 in the US.

pages.title: DR-024 Pricing is metered, and the tail is priced
pages.summary: Subscriptions carry a stated monthly allowance rather than an unlimited promise, the consequential tier is priced explicitly, and a merchant may never pay for placement in a recommendation.

pages.title: Decisions
pages.summary: The ledger of decision records: every decision that shapes AI.fred, with what was rejected, what each closes off, its status and its trigger where it is amber.

pages.title: AI.fred Dependency Map
pages.summary: The dependency map of the record (DR-017) served as a three-dimensional view: every decision, mechanism, invariant and closed list, with the cone of change for any node. Generated from tools/depmap/graph.json by the map's own tool, committed, and failed by the harness when stale; the one page outside the page floor, by DR-010's exception.
